_doc: Cortex BEAM-100K retrieval-proxy baseline. The TS port must reproduce this score within tolerance. METRIC: a RETRIEVAL-PROXY MRR (NOT BEAM's published end-to-end LLM-as-judge nugget score). RR(q)=1/rank(m*) where m* is the first retrieved memory whose content substring-matches the gold answer (len>2) or an 80-char gold source-turn prefix; abstention is special (RR=1 iff retrieval empty OR top score<0.3, else 0). AGGREGATION: nested macro-average — per-conversation per-ability MRR (miss=0), mean over conversations per ability, mean over abilities = overall (cortex main benchmarks/beam/run_benchmark.py:258-419). Dataset: BEAM 100K split (Tavakoli et al., ICLR 2026), Mohammadta/BEAM HuggingFace, 20 conversations, 10 abilities; 394 evaluated questions (40 abstention always kept + non-abstention questions carrying source_chat_ids; non-abstention without source ids skipped exactly as the Python oracle does). BASELINE PROVENANCE (CORRECTED 2026-06-22): the value below (0.5006) is the OBSERVED output of the Python oracle's own run_benchmark.py evaluate_retrieval on the FULL 20-conv HF dataset (db.recall top_k=10 domain=beam, cortex main, clean cortex_bench DB), measured 2026-06-22 — i.e. the reproducible same-harness target for the TS port. The previously-recorded 0.591 was taken from the arxiv papers (docs/arxiv-thermodynamic/main.pdf Table tab:benchmarks + docs/arxiv-context-assembly/main.tex:167) and is NOT reproducible by run_benchmark.py on current cortex main — the Cortex retrieval code has drifted since the paper snapshot (the paper number is a frozen historical artifact, not a live target). Gating the TS port against 0.591 measures the Cortex paper-vs-code drift, NOT TS fidelity; gating against the oracle-reproduced 0.5006 is the correct apples-to-apples parity check. KEY PER-ABILITY FACT: abstention scores 0.1500 in BOTH the Python oracle and the TS port (identical by construction) — the <0.3 abstention gate fires on the same 6/40 questions in both; the other 34 get blended top-score ~0.70 because FlashRank's cross-encoder rates topical-but-irrelevant passages high (blended=0.3*wrrf(~0.017)+0.7*ce(~1.0)≈0.70>0.30). This is faithful behaviour, not a bug. by_category below holds the Python-oracle per-ability MRRs for reference (NOT gated; overall MRR is the only load-bearing metric).
dataset: BEAM 100K split (Mohammadta/BEAM, 20 conversations, 394 evaluated questions, 10 abilities)

captured_from.method: benchmarks/beam/run_benchmark.py evaluate_retrieval, full 20-conv HF dataset, clean cortex_bench DB, db.recall(top_k=10, domain=beam) — same code path the TS cortex-beam-pg runner mirrors
